# Application persistence

Read when implementing repositories, transactions, or application-owned migration files. Live query,
lock, migration-execution, and recovery work belongs to `database-reliability`.

- Match the selected engine, driver, ORM/query layer, migration tool, and pool already established.
  Do not impose PostgreSQL or replace a repository's data model from this reference.
- Keep transaction boundaries explicit and short wherever an invariant spans writes. Never hold a
  database transaction across an outbound network call.
- Enforce uniqueness and referential invariants in the database; translate expected conflicts at the
  application boundary. Parameterize every value and bound result sets.
- Size pools from the database/service limits and total application concurrency, not a copied default.
  Release connections on cancellation/error and test pool exhaustion and transaction cleanup.
- Add migrations; never rewrite a migration already applied outside disposable development. Use
  additive compatibility steps for shared schemas.
- Every migration has a recovery procedure. A down script is included only when it is demonstrably
  lossless for the allowed state; forward repair or restore/PITR may be safer after new writes.
